label: Animation
definition: The craft of making drawn, modelled or computer-generated images appear to move and perform.
activity: Watch a feature or a programme of animated shorts at a free Yale screening (Films at the Whitney, Yale Film Archive), or study scenes frame by frame at home, noting how the animator builds a thought before an action.
actorUse: Character work and physical expression: animators are trained in acting theory (Ed Hooks' Acting for Animators applies Stanislavski to animated performance), so studying animation in reverse shows an actor how a clear thought precedes and shapes a gesture, and how exaggeration reads.
notes: The pedagogy runs animator-from-acting, not actor-from-animation; the reverse use is an inference. Films at the Whitney is free and open to all, but whether animation is programmed in a given term varies.

label: Art Direction
definition: The design and supervision of a film's or production's visual world: sets, locations, palette and the look of every space on screen.
activity: Visit the free Yale School of Architecture Gallery or the Yale Center for British Art and study how interiors and rooms are composed, then rewatch a film scene at home and list what the set tells you about who lives there.
actorUse: Script analysis and character work: reading the designed environment as given circumstances (Uta Hagen's 'where' work and Shurtleff's 'Place' guidepost both ask the actor to make the place specific).
notes: Shurtleff's 'Place' guidepost is real; tying art direction study to it is an inference, not a documented exercise.

label: Casting
definition: The process of choosing performers for roles, run by casting directors through auditions, self-tapes and callbacks.
activity: Read audition sides for a current role and work them through Michael Shurtleff's twelve guideposts, then record a self-tape on a phone in a dorm room or library study room.
actorUse: Audition technique and script analysis: Shurtleff, a Broadway casting director, wrote Audition to show actors what casting looks for; his guideposts (relationship, conflict, the moment before, discoveries, place, etc.) are widely taught.
notes: Activity source is the book itself (available through libraries); no New Haven venue needed.

label: Choreography
definition: The composition and arrangement of movement and dance for performance.
activity: Take a drop-in dance class at Payne Whitney Gym (membership is free for full-time Yale students) or learn a short combination and break it down with Laban effort qualities.
actorUse: Movement and dance: Laban Movement Analysis, a choreographer's system, has been used in actor movement training for over half a century (Yat Malmgren, Jean Newlove) to find a character's physical life; the Yale acting plan of study includes Movement I and 'Character Analysis and Movement'.
notes: Group fitness classes may require a class pass on top of free gym membership.

label: Cinematography
definition: The art of photographing a film: framing, lens, camera movement and light.
activity: Attend a free 35mm screening from the Yale Film Archive and note shot sizes, or join a no-experience-needed CCAM C-CAMP cinematography workshop at Yale.
actorUse: On-camera work: knowing frame size tells the actor how much to scale a performance; Michael Caine's Acting in Film is built on adjusting to the lens (e.g. stillness and not blinking in close-up). The Yale plan of study includes On-Camera Acting Technique.
notes: CCAM C-CAMP workshops listed cinematography in the event found; availability varies by term (https://filmnet.yalecollege.yale.edu/event/ccam-presents-c-camp).

label: Color Grading
definition: The post-production adjustment of a film's colour and contrast to set mood and continuity.
activity: Watch a film at a free Yale screening paying attention to colour mood, or try a CCAM editing/post workshop at Yale.
actorUse: Imagination: noticing how colour carries a scene's mood can feed Michael Chekhov's 'atmosphere' work, where the actor imagines and radiates the emotional atmosphere of a scene.
notes: No acting pedagogy links grading directly to actor training; this is the weakest craft link. I did not confirm a grading-specific CCAM workshop.

label: Costume Design
definition: The design of clothing worn by performers to reveal character, period and status.
activity: Study dress, posture and fabric in period portraits at the free Yale Center for British Art or Yale University Art Gallery, then rehearse a speech in a long skirt, coat or heeled shoe to feel what it does to the body.
actorUse: Period/classical text and physical character work: Stanislavski's Building a Character discusses how external means (costume, carriage) feed the inner character; period dress changes posture and tempo.
notes: Building a Character covers external characterisation broadly; that it explicitly treats costume is from my knowledge of the book, not verified on the cited page.

label: Creature Effects
definition: Practical and digital techniques for creating monsters, animals and non-human beings on screen and stage.
activity: Sketch and observe the animal dioramas at the free Yale Peabody Museum, then work out how a creature's weight and rhythm would move in a human body.
actorUse: Physical expression and movement: Lecoq's first-year curriculum is built on observing animals and the natural world and embodying them, the same skill creature performers use under suits or prosthetics.
notes: Link is via animal/creature embodiment, not effects technology itself.

label: Dialect Coaching
definition: Coaching performers in accents and dialects for specific roles.
activity: Listen to primary-source speakers on the free International Dialects of English Archive and drill one accent with Knight-Thompson 'Four Ps' (people, prosody, posture, pronunciation).
actorUse: Accents and vocal expression: IDEA was founded by voice coach Paul Meier to give actors real-life accent models; Knight-Thompson Speechwork is a skills-based speech and accent training for actors. The Yale plan of study includes Speech and Accents I-III.

label: Directing
definition: Leading the interpretation and staging of a play or film and guiding the performers.
activity: See a Yale Cabaret or Yale Rep production (student tickets) and afterward write down the staging choices; or read Bogart and Landau's The Viewpoints Book in the library.
actorUse: Script analysis, ensemble and spatial awareness: Viewpoints, developed for actors and directors, trains shared physical vocabulary and awareness of spatial relationship and composition.
notes: Yale Rep offers discounted student tickets and student rush; Yale Cabaret student price about $12 (not free).

label: Editing
definition: Selecting and assembling shots into a film's final sequence and rhythm.
activity: Read Walter Murch's In the Blink of an Eye from the library and rewatch a scene noting where each cut falls relative to the actor's blinks and thoughts.
actorUse: On-camera work: Murch argues emotion is the first priority of a cut and that a good actor's blinks track their thoughts (he noted Gene Hackman's blinks marked good cut points), teaching the actor that thought must be continuous and readable.
notes: Hackman anecdote from secondary summaries of the book.

label: Film Criticism
definition: The analysis and evaluation of films in writing or speech.
activity: Watch a free Films at the Whitney screening and write a 500-word review focusing on one performance.
actorUse: Script analysis and discernment: articulating why a performance works trains the analytical half of the craft; the Yale plan of study includes Text Analysis I and II.
notes: No pedagogy source found specifically connecting criticism-writing to actor development.

label: Film Festivals
definition: Curated events that premiere and showcase films, often with filmmaker Q&As.
activity: Attend free screenings at NHdocs, the New Haven Documentary Film Festival, held at the New Haven Free Public Library and Yale venues.
actorUse: Observation and emotional depth: documentaries offer real people's speech and behaviour as raw material, the observation of life that Lecoq and Stanislavski-based training rely on.
notes: NHdocs moved from June to October around 2022; check year's dates. Link from documentary viewing to observation training is inference.

label: Film History
definition: The study of cinema's development, movements and landmark works.
activity: Attend 'Treasures from the Yale Film Archive', a free year-round series of classic films in 35mm with introductions and printed notes.
actorUse: Character work and range: studying performance styles across eras shows how acting conventions change; useful for period pieces. Caine's Acting in Film and similar texts draw on this lineage.
notes: Plausible but no specific pedagogy source located.

label: Film Preservation
definition: The work of saving, restoring and archiving film materials.
activity: Attend a free Yale Film Archive screening and read about the Archive's preservation projects (it holds 7,000+ 35mm/16mm titles and is a FIAF associate).
actorUse: Period research: archival prints are a primary source for how people moved and spoke in earlier decades.
notes: Very weak direct link to actor craft; better treated as a film-history/observation pursuit.

label: Film Scoring
definition: Composing music written to accompany and shape a film's drama.
activity: Listen to a film score with headphones and map where the music changes tempo against the scene, or attend a free Yale School of Music concert.
actorUse: Tempo-rhythm and imagination: Stanislavski's tempo-rhythm work (Building a Character) uses musical impulse to shape inner state and movement; recovery: music listening aids stress recovery (PLOS ONE 2022 meta-analysis).
notes: Recovery source: https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0270031

label: Foley
definition: Recording everyday sound effects such as footsteps and cloth to sync with picture.
activity: Record ordinary actions (footsteps, a cup set down) on a phone and match them to a muted film clip.
actorUse: Object work and listening: Foley requires exact re-creation of how an action sounds, close to Uta Hagen's object exercises, which build awareness of the specific physical behaviour of everyday actions.
notes: No public New Haven Foley resource found; activity is home practice. Link to Hagen is analogy.

label: Hair And Makeup
definition: Styling hair and applying makeup or prosthetics to create a character's look.
activity: Practise a character or ageing makeup from Richard Corson's Stage Makeup textbook in front of a mirror.
actorUse: Character work: stage actors often apply their own makeup; Corson's text, long called the standard in theatre makeup courses, covers character creation and ageing for performers.
notes: Whether the Yale acting curriculum includes makeup was not confirmed.

label: Improvisation
definition: Performing without a script, building scenes spontaneously from offers.
activity: Watch a free Yale improv show (Exit Players, Purple Crayon, Improvaganza) or play Spolin theatre games with classmates.
actorUse: Spontaneity, listening and responsiveness: Viola Spolin's theatre games, codified in Improvisation for the Theater, are a system of actor training built on point of concentration and spontaneity.

label: Intimacy Coordination
definition: Choreographing intimate or sexual scenes with consent-based practice to protect performers.
activity: Read the five-pillar framework (context, consent, communication, choreography, closure) and practise boundary conversations with a scene partner.
actorUse: Composure and safety: consent and closure practices let actors play intimate scenes repeatably and step out of role afterward; the Yale acting plan of study includes 'Acting Intimacy and Combat for the Stage'.
notes: The pillars are attributed to Intimacy Directors International (2016); I saw them in search summaries, not by reading the cited page in full.

label: Lighting
definition: Designing and controlling light for stage or screen.
activity: At a Yale Rep or Cabaret performance, watch where actors stand to find light; or note how window light falls across faces in YUAG portraits.
actorUse: Stage and on-camera technique: 'finding your light' and hitting marks are working skills; Caine's Acting in Film covers screen technical awareness.
notes: I did not verify that Caine's book discusses lighting specifically.

label: Location Scouting
definition: Finding and assessing real places to film.
activity: Walk New Haven (East Rock, the Green, Wooster Square) photographing places where a scene from a current play could happen.
actorUse: Imagination and given circumstances: making the place of a scene specific (Shurtleff's 'Place' guidepost; Hagen's 'where').
notes: Analogy; also gets the walking/nature benefit if outdoors.

label: Miniatures
definition: Building small-scale models of sets, vehicles or landscapes for filming or design.
activity: Build a cardboard model box of a play's set at a desk, or use the free Ives Squared makerspace at the New Haven Free Public Library.
actorUse: Recovery: hands-on craft is associated with better mood and life satisfaction (Frontiers in Public Health 2024, 7,182 adults); also lets the actor plan blocking in the set's space.
notes: Craft study is cross-sectional; it shows association, not cause. Ives Squared programme details not verified.

label: Motion Capture
definition: Recording a performer's movement with sensors and cameras to drive a digital character.
activity: Join a CCAM motion-capture workshop at Yale (Vicon studio in the CCAM Leeds Studio; introductory workshops are offered).
actorUse: Physical expression and imagination: drama schools now teach performance capture as acting (LAMDA's Motion Capture for Performance combines its movement and acting techniques with mocap).
notes: CCAM workshop listings are per-event; schedule varies.

label: Music Supervision
definition: Selecting and licensing existing music for a film or show.
activity: Build a playlist for a character in a current role and listen to it during preparation.
actorUse: Emotional preparation and tempo: musical impulse to shape inner state echoes Stanislavski's tempo-rhythm exercises; music listening also aids stress recovery.
notes: Character playlists are a common actor habit but I found no pedagogy text that names the practice.

label: Practical Effects
definition: Physical, in-camera effects such as rigs, squibs, breakaways and atmospheric smoke.
activity: Read about and watch behind-the-scenes material on practical effects; or try simple builds at the library makerspace.
actorUse: Composure and safety on set: understanding effects lets the actor react truthfully and safely; Uta Hagen's endowment exercise (giving an object qualities it lacks) is the acting tool for fake blood, breakaway glass etc.
notes: Hands-on effects (pyro, squibs) are not appropriate spare-time activity; activity is study only.

label: Producing
definition: Organising the money, people and schedule that get a production made.
activity: Help produce a Yale Cabaret show or a classmate's reading: book a room, schedule rehearsals, print programmes.
actorUse: Discipline and self-generated work: the Yale acting training progresses toward 'self-generated performance', which requires producing one's own work.
notes: Cabaret is entirely student-run; whether acting students take producing roles is not confirmed but plausible.

label: Production Design
definition: Overall visual design of a production's world, sets and spaces.
activity: Visit the free Yale School of Architecture Gallery (Rudolph Hall) and see student design work; sketch a set for a scene.
actorUse: Given circumstances and spatial awareness: Viewpoints treats architecture and topography as performance material.
notes: The gallery's name and hours vary by source (Art and Architecture Gallery / Yale School of Architecture Gallery).

label: Props
definition: Objects handled by performers on stage or screen.
activity: Rehearse Uta Hagen's basic object exercise: two minutes of a real daily routine, with real objects, for an hour.
actorUse: Object work and focus: Hagen's object exercises build awareness of specific physical behaviour and endowment of objects.

label: Puppetry
definition: Bringing puppets and objects to life through manipulation and voice.
activity: Practise animating a found object (a sock, a paper bag) to breathe, look and react, in a dorm room or with classmates.
actorUse: Physical expression, focus and ensemble: published actor-education research examines object animation in actor training ('Actor education, object animation and care', Theatre, Dance and Performance Training, 2022).
notes: I could not open the article (403); title and journal from search results and DOI prefix only. No New Haven puppetry venue verified (UConn's Ballard Institute is in Storrs, requires travel).

label: Screenwriting
definition: Writing scripts for film and television.
activity: Write a two-page scene, then read it aloud with a classmate.
actorUse: Script analysis: writing scenes teaches how objectives, obstacles and events are built, the same units the Yale plan's Text Analysis courses teach actors to find.
notes: Source confirms text analysis is in the curriculum, not that screenwriting improves it.

label: Script Supervision
definition: Tracking continuity, dialogue and coverage on a film set.
activity: Film the same short action three times on a phone and check whether props, hands and lines match between takes.
actorUse: On-camera work: matching action and business across takes is a core screen skill; the Yale plan includes On-Camera Acting Technique.
notes: Source shows on-camera training exists, not continuity specifically.

label: Set Decoration
definition: Dressing a set with furniture, objects and details that make it lived in.
activity: Look at furnished period rooms and interiors depicted at the Yale Center for British Art, listing what each object says about its owner.
actorUse: Character work and endowment: an actor's relationship to the objects in a room (Hagen's endowment) makes a set feel lived in.
notes: Analogy.

label: Showrunning
definition: Running a television series as head writer and executive producer.
activity: Watch a full season arc of a TV drama and chart how each character changes episode to episode.
actorUse: Script analysis over long arcs: series acting requires tracking a character across many episodes.
notes: No pedagogy source; weakest along with title design and colour grading.

label: Sound Design
definition: Creating and arranging a production's soundscape, effects and atmosphere.
activity: Sit in a park or café for 30 minutes with eyes closed and list every sound; or listen to a radio drama.
actorUse: Listening and atmosphere: Chekhov's atmosphere work and attentive listening both depend on sensitivity to the sound of a space.
notes: Inference.

label: Sound Mixing
definition: Balancing dialogue, music and effects into a final soundtrack.
activity: Record a monologue on a phone at different distances and levels and listen back.
actorUse: Vocal expression for microphone: the Yale plan includes 'audio' (camera and audio) training; hearing oneself recorded calibrates mic technique.
notes: The Yale school describes training including 'camera and audio' (search summary of drama.yale.edu).

label: Stage Combat
definition: The safe, choreographed staging of violence for performance.
activity: Run slow-tempo unarmed drills (slaps, falls, knaps) with a classmate, as taught in class.
actorUse: Stage combat, movement and safety: Yale's acting plan includes 'Acting Intimacy and Combat for the Stage' and 'Advanced Principles of Acting Stage Combat'; SAFD-style training emphasises accuracy and safety.
notes: Drills should be only material already taught, never improvised contact.

label: Storyboarding
definition: Drawing a film's shots in sequence before shooting.
activity: Storyboard a monologue as six panels in a sketchbook.
actorUse: Imagination: visualising images behind the text, as Chekhov's technique asks the actor to see the imagined images.
notes: Inference.

label: Stunts
definition: Performing dangerous physical action safely for film or stage.
activity: Do strength and conditioning at Payne Whitney Gym; practise only stage falls already taught in combat class.
actorUse: Stamina, movement and safety: physical conditioning and combat technique; Yale trains stage combat.
notes: Real stunt work needs a coordinator; activity limited to conditioning.

label: Title Design
definition: Designing a film's opening and closing title sequences.
activity: Watch title sequences and note how they set a film's tone.
actorUse: Tone: noticing how a film announces its genre may help an actor pitch a performance.
notes: No credible actor-development link found.

label: Visual Effects
definition: Digitally created or composited imagery added to filmed footage.
activity: Practise reacting to an imagined creature or environment against a blank wall and film it.
actorUse: Imagination: green-screen acting requires imagining an environment that isn't there (the 'magic if').
notes: The cited paper is on academia.edu; I did not verify publication venue.

label: Voice Acting
definition: Performing characters with the voice alone, for animation, games, audio drama or narration.
activity: Read a chapter aloud into a phone recorder after a Linklater voice warm-up.
actorUse: Vocal expression: Linklater's Freeing the Natural Voice is a standard actor voice text; Yale's plan includes Voice I-III.

label: Writers’ Rooms
definition: Collaborative teams writing a television series together.
activity: Join classmates to pitch and improvise scene ideas.
actorUse: Listening and collaboration: idea-building in a room shares improv's 'yes, and' logic.
notes: Analogy.

label: Animals
definition: Interest in animals and their behaviour.
activity: Observe squirrels, dogs and birds in East Rock Park or the animal dioramas at the free Yale Peabody Museum, then embody one.
actorUse: Physical expression and character work: animal study is in Lecoq's first-year curriculum (observation of animals and the natural world).

label: Art
definition: Interest in painting, sculpture and visual art.
activity: Spend an hour with a few works at the free Yale University Art Gallery or Yale Center for British Art.
actorUse: Imagination and character visualisation; recovery: a brief gallery visit lowered cortisol and self-reported stress (Clow & Fredhoi 2006), and a scoping review supports art viewing for stress.
notes: The Clow study was small (n=25), uncontrolled.

label: Cars
definition: Interest in automobiles: their design, engineering, history and driving culture.
activity: Read automotive history or design books from the New Haven Free Public Library, or watch films with driving scenes and note how the actors handle the car; on a New Haven street, watch how different people get in and out of cars and carry themselves at the wheel.
actorUse: Observation and physical character work: how a person handles a machine reveals status and temperament, the kind of everyday-behaviour observation that Lecoq's first-year 'observation of the world' and Hagen's object work rely on; on-camera driving scenes are also a practical screen skill.
notes: Hardest interest to connect credibly. No acting-pedagogy source ties cars to actor training, and the brief rules out car ownership and travel. The observation link is an analogy.

label: Cooking
definition: Preparing food.
activity: Cook a meal in a shared kitchen paying full sensory attention, then re-create it as a Hagen object exercise.
actorUse: Sensory recall and object work: Hagen's basic object exercise uses daily routines (e.g. making breakfast) with real props.

label: Design
definition: Interest in how objects, buildings, spaces and graphics are designed.
activity: Visit the free Yale School of Architecture Gallery in Rudolph Hall (180 York St) for an exhibition, then walk the building noticing how its spaces make you move.
actorUse: Spatial awareness and physical expression: the Viewpoints method (Bogart and Landau) treats architecture, shape and spatial relationship as material the actor responds to.
notes: Gallery listed as free, open Mon-Sat, by Visit New Haven; check current exhibitions at architecture.yale.edu.

label: Fashion
definition: Interest in clothing, style and how people present themselves through dress.
activity: Study dress, and how it shapes posture, in portraits at the free Yale Center for British Art or Yale University Art Gallery, then people-watch on Chapel Street noting what clothing signals.
actorUse: Character work and social status: Brecht's gestus asks the actor to make a character's social class and relations visible in outward bearing; dress is one of the clearest carriers of that.
notes: Gestus concerns socially encoded gesture and attitude; extending it to clothing is my inference. The costume_design entry covers the period-movement angle.

label: Film
definition: Interest in watching and thinking about films.
activity: Attend a Films at the Whitney or Yale Film Archive 35mm screening at the Whitney Humanities Center (53 Wall St), all free and open to the public.
actorUse: On-camera work: watching screen acting with attention to scale, stillness and the eyes, the technique Michael Caine sets out in Acting in Film; the Yale acting plan includes On-Camera Acting Technique.
notes: Watching films as study is common advice; no controlled evidence that viewing improves screen acting.

label: Fitness
definition: Exercise and physical conditioning for strength, endurance and health.
activity: Train at Payne Whitney Gym (membership is automatic and free for full-time Yale students): a run, a cycling or yoga class, or strength work.
actorUse: Stamina and recovery: conditioning supports the physically demanding movement and combat training in the Yale plan; reviews find exercise reduces anxiety symptoms, though trial quality is mixed.
notes: Stubbs et al. 2017 (Psychiatry Research) found the anxiolytic effect depended heavily on control condition and five of six RCTs were low quality. No pedagogy text found quantifying stamina for actors. Group classes may need a paid pass.

label: Games
definition: Interest in board, card, party and video games.
activity: Play Spolin or Boal theatre games with classmates, or drop in on the free Go Club or chess club at the New Haven Free Public Library's Ives Main Library.
actorUse: Spontaneity, listening and responsiveness: Spolin's theatre games and Boal's Games for Actors and Non-Actors are both actor-training systems built from play.
notes: The link holds for theatre games; board and video games themselves have no established acting benefit. NHFPL Go/chess clubs are from a search summary, not a page I read.

label: History
definition: Interest in the past: events, people and how they lived.
activity: Visit the free Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library exhibition hall (Gutenberg Bible, Audubon's Birds of America, rotating exhibitions; no reservation) and research the period of a play in rehearsal.
actorUse: Period and classical text: grounding a period play's given circumstances; the Yale plan's 'Acting II: Plays of Extended and Heightened Language' covers Shakespeare and verse drama.
notes: Source confirms period/verse work is in the curriculum; that historical research aids it is standard dramaturgical practice, not a measured claim.

label: Music
definition: Interest in listening to, playing or singing music.
activity: Attend a free Yale School of Music student recital or Lunchtime Chamber Music concert in Sprague Hall, or practise singing.
actorUse: Singing and tempo-rhythm, plus recovery: the Yale plan includes Singing and Acting Through Song; Stanislavski's tempo-rhythm work uses musical impulse; a 2022 PLOS ONE meta-analysis found music listening aids stress recovery in healthy people.
notes: Most YSM concerts are free; some series are ticketed. de Witte et al. 2020 (Health Psychology Review, 104 RCTs) is a second supporting meta-analysis.

label: Nature
definition: Interest in the outdoors, landscape and the natural world.
activity: Walk the trails of East Rock Park (427 acres; summit open on foot Mon-Sat) for about 90 minutes.
actorUse: Recovery and composure: a 90-minute walk in a natural setting reduced self-reported rumination and subgenual prefrontal cortex activity, versus an urban walk (Bratman et al. 2015, PNAS 112:8567-8572).
notes: Single study with a small sample; the direction is consistent with wider nature-exposure literature.

label: Photography
definition: Interest in taking and studying photographs.
activity: Book the Yale University Art Gallery's James E. Duffy Study Room (about 5,000 photographs; free, by written appointment two weeks ahead) to study portraits, or photograph public places around New Haven.
actorUse: Observation for character: studying how real people hold themselves feeds the observation of life on which Lecoq's first year is built.
notes: Photographing strangers raises consent issues; portrait study is the safer activity.

label: Politics
definition: Interest in government, public affairs and argument.
activity: Attend a Yale Political Union Tuesday-evening debate, usually free and open to the Yale community, with a guest keynote and floor speeches.
actorUse: Rhetoric and social analysis: watching live persuasion trains the ear for argument in text; Brecht's gestus asks actors to make a character's social and political position visible.
notes: YPU debates are described as open to the Yale community, not confirmed open to the general public (fine for an enrolled student).

label: Reading
definition: Interest in reading books, especially fiction and drama.
activity: Read a novel or play for an hour at the New Haven Free Public Library or a Yale library.
actorUse: Emotional depth and character work: a meta-analysis found fiction reading has a small positive causal effect on social cognition (Dodell-Feder & Tamir 2018, Journal of Experimental Psychology: General 147(11):1713-1727).
notes: Effect small (g about 0.15); a p-curve analysis (Quinlan et al. 2020) questioned the evidential value of brief-exposure studies.

label: Sport
definition: Interest in playing or following sport.
activity: Play a pickup game or swim at Payne Whitney Gym (free for full-time Yale students).
actorUse: Movement and physical expression: Jacques Lecoq came to theatre from sport and sports rehabilitation, and his movement analysis grew from athletic gesture; also stamina.
notes: Specific PWG sports offerings (pickup, pool) not individually verified.

label: Technology
definition: Interest in computers, gadgets and digital media tools.
activity: Set up and test a phone self-tape rig (light, sound, framing), or take a no-experience-needed CCAM workshop in motion capture, projection mapping or video editing at Yale.
actorUse: On-camera and performance-capture work: self-taping is now routine for auditions; LAMDA teaches motion capture for performance.
notes: Self-tape as industry norm is common knowledge, not sourced here.

label: Television
definition: Interest in watching and following television series.
activity: Watch an episode of a TV drama and track one character's objective scene by scene.
actorUse: On-camera work and script analysis over a series arc; screen technique as in Caine's Acting in Film.
notes: No New Haven venue needed; no specific pedagogy for TV viewing.

label: Theater
definition: Interest in seeing and making live theatre.
activity: See a Yale Repertory Theatre production on a student ticket or half-price rush, or a show at the student-run Yale Cabaret (217 Park St, about $12 for students).
actorUse: Craft in general, especially listening and presence: watching peers and professionals is how actors absorb conventions and range.
notes: Activity is well sourced; the developmental claim is common practice without a single citable source.

label: Travel
definition: Interest in travel and other places and cultures.
activity: Without travelling: listen to speakers from other regions on the free International Dialects of English Archive and read travel writing from the library.
actorUse: Accents and cultural specificity: Knight-Thompson Speechwork's 'Four Ps' start from People, treating accents as they exist in the world.
notes: Hard to connect because travel itself is excluded; this is a substitute pursuit.

label: Writing
definition: Interest in writing: journals, fiction, essays or scripts.
activity: Write for 15-20 minutes about a stressful experience (expressive writing), or write a character biography for a current role.
actorUse: Recovery and character work: Pennebaker's expressive-writing paradigm; Frattaroli's 2006 meta-analysis (146 studies, Psychological Bulletin) found a small significant benefit (d = 0.15) on psychological and health outcomes. Character biographies are a common acting-class tool.
notes: Effect is small; larger for more stressed participants. The Frattaroli figures are from search summaries of secondary sources.
